title: Agroforestry practices — Riparian forest buffers
claim: Riparian forest buffers — streamside plantings of trees, shrubs, and grasses — buffer non-point source pollution of waterways from adjacent land and reduce streambank erosion, while also enhancing wildlife habitat.
evidence_text: FAO's Sustainable Forest Management Toolbox describes riparian forest buffers as natural or re-established streamside plantings of trees, shrubs, and grasses that buffer non-point source pollution of waterways from adjacent land and reduce streambank erosion. Beyond water-quality protection, these buffers provide wildlife habitat enhancement and, in some designs, opportunities for compatible product harvesting alongside their conservation function.
